notes.C01: Exact event logs for own screen repros beat pixel inference, but needs recorder/tool integration to keep up.
notes.C02: Pixel-to-action-script with lag and test compile is ambitious; cursor/ripple detection is a hard breakthrough.
notes.C03: Cheap one-image motion encoding from existing signals; falsifiable, but unproven that vision models read it.
notes.C04: Directly fills the named audio gap with text and spectrogram at low cost; concrete and benchable.
notes.C05: Audio-visual sync anchors give real cause-effect dating, but depends on clean audio and detectors.
notes.C06: Before/after pairs plus a foveated look cut image tokens and address temporal questions with existing signals.
notes.C07: Lazy question-driven sensing saves work, but cache/log/learned router adds state and tuning surface.
notes.C08: Best answer to daily-use friction via a hook with tiers and a receipt; many moving parts to maintain.
notes.C09: Synthetic ground-truth bench proves every claim cheaply and doubles as self-test; high leverage.
notes.C10: Honest card with declared gaps and kill rule builds trust and discipline, but is a format more than a sensor.
notes.C11: Metered cloud valve is allowed but adds ongoing cost, egress and a monitor; opt-in limits the damage.
notes.C12: Subagent viewing shifts tokens rather than saving them, adds orchestration and per-use cost.
notes.C13: Narrow priming defence with little evidence it matters for this agent; low value.
notes.C14: Slow-change detector is a real blind spot but a niche add-on to the pair detector.
notes.C15: Saliency-based budgeting is a plausible tweak, not a new capability; thin on specifics.
